Science & Learning · Clinical Nutrition

Obesity & insulin resistance

Mechanisms, clinical relevance, nutrition care and evidence — with visual explanations.

Obesity is a chronic, multifactorial disease

Excess or abnormal adiposity can impair health. Energy balance is regulated by interacting biological, genetic, behavioural, psychological, social and environmental factors. BMI is a screening measure; it does not directly measure visceral fat or fully describe health.

Adipose tissue is an endocrine organ

Adipocytes store triglycerides and release adipokines and other mediators. In dysfunctional adipose tissue, altered adipokine signalling, increased lipolysis, ectopic lipid deposition and low-grade inflammation may contribute to metabolic dysfunction.

Insulin resistance (IR)

IR is a reduced biological response to insulin in target tissues. The pancreas may compensate with increased insulin secretion (compensatory hyperinsulinaemia) before glucose regulation deteriorates in some people.

Three key target tissues

Skeletal muscle: reduced insulin-stimulated glucose uptake. Liver: inadequate suppression of hepatic glucose production. Adipose tissue: impaired suppression of lipolysis, increasing circulating free fatty acids.

Visual 1 · How insulin resistance links fat tissue, liver and muscle

Interpretation

Adipose tissue dysfunction can increase free-fatty-acid flux and inflammatory signalling. The liver may release more glucose, while skeletal muscle takes up less glucose in response to insulin. These tissues interact; this diagram is a simplified teaching model, not a complete molecular pathway.

Evidence: Petersen & Shulman, Physiological Reviews (2018), Mechanisms of Insulin Action and Insulin Resistance.

Visual 2 · Insulin signalling in skeletal muscle

In insulin-sensitive muscle, insulin receptor signalling through IRS–PI3K–Akt promotes GLUT4 translocation and glucose uptake. In insulin resistance, this response is blunted; exercise can also stimulate muscle glucose uptake through partly insulin-independent pathways.

Further reading: Insulin Resistance: From Mechanisms to Therapeutic Strategies.

Clinical deep dive · From adiposity to metabolic complications

1. Adipose tissue dysfunction

With adipocyte hypertrophy and impaired adipose expandability, lipid storage becomes less metabolically flexible. Increased lipolysis can raise circulating free fatty acids (FFAs), while altered adipokines and immune-cell signalling contribute to low-grade inflammation. These processes can promote ectopic lipid accumulation in liver and skeletal muscle.

2. Hepatic insulin resistance

Insulin becomes less effective at suppressing hepatic gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis. The liver may continue releasing glucose despite fed-state insulin, contributing to fasting hyperglycaemia. Hepatic de novo lipogenesis and VLDL-triglyceride production may also be increased.

3. Skeletal muscle insulin resistance

Muscle is a major site of insulin-stimulated postprandial glucose disposal. Impaired IRS–PI3K–Akt signalling can reduce GLUT4 translocation to the cell membrane and reduce glucose uptake and glycogen synthesis.

4. Pancreatic compensation

Pancreatic β-cells may initially compensate by increasing insulin secretion. In susceptible individuals, progressive β-cell dysfunction means compensation becomes insufficient; dysglycaemia and type 2 diabetes may develop. Progression is variable and not inevitable.

Clinical relevance: obesity and insulin resistance are associated with type 2 diabetes, MASLD, dyslipidaemia, hypertension, obstructive sleep apnoea and cardiovascular risk. Risk is heterogeneous; assess the person, not BMI alone.

Nutrition therapy

Individualised energy intake, adequate protein, high-fibre carbohydrate sources, unsaturated fats, vegetables, legumes and whole fruit. No single macro split is best for everyone.

Physical activity

Muscle contraction improves glucose uptake and fitness. Combine aerobic activity with resistance exercise, adjusted to capacity and medical context.

Sleep & behaviour

Sleep quality, stress, medicines, food access, culture and environment influence metabolic health and adherence.

Clinical assessment · ABCD

Laboratory Tests & Metabolic Risk

Core investigations are not an optional side note: they help assess glycaemia, cardiometabolic complications and overall clinical context.

Clinical principle: insulin resistance itself is not diagnosed by one universally accepted routine blood test. FPG, HbA1c and OGTT assess dysglycaemia; fasting insulin/HOMA-IR are surrogate estimates with assay- and population-dependent cut-offs. A clinician chooses tests based on history, examination and risk.

1 · Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG)

Why it matters: measures fasting glycaemia and helps screen/diagnose prediabetes and diabetes. Usually requires ≥8 hours fasting (water allowed).

Non-pregnant adult ADA 2026: Normal <100 mg/dL · Prediabetes 100–125 · Diabetes ≥126. In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycaemia, confirm with repeat/second abnormal test.

2 · HbA1c

Why it matters: estimates average glycaemia over roughly 2–3 months; no fasting generally required.

ADA 2026: Normal <5.7% · Prediabetes 5.7–6.4% · Diabetes ≥6.5% (standardised laboratory method). Anaemia, haemoglobin variants, altered red-cell turnover, pregnancy and some conditions may affect interpretation.

3 · 75-g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT)

Why it matters: measures the 2-hour glucose response after a standard 75-g glucose load; can identify impaired glucose tolerance missed by fasting glucose in some cases.

2-hour plasma glucose: Normal <140 mg/dL · Prediabetes 140–199 · Diabetes ≥200.

4 · Fasting Insulin & HOMA-IR

Why it matters: can estimate fasting insulin resistance in research/selected clinical contexts. HOMA-IR is not a stand-alone diagnostic test and thresholds vary by assay, ethnicity, age and population. Do not interpret it in isolation.

Calculator available in Clinical Calculators.

5 · Lipid Profile

Total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C and triglycerides help assess cardiometabolic risk. IR/central adiposity may be associated with high triglycerides and low HDL-C, but the pattern is not diagnostic by itself.

6 · Liver assessment (ALT, AST ± additional tests)

Considered when clinically indicated to assess liver injury and possible metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Enzymes can be normal despite steatosis; results need clinical interpretation.

7 · Other tests according to the person

Blood pressure, renal function (creatinine/eGFR, urine albumin where indicated), thyroid tests if symptoms/history suggest, pregnancy status where relevant, and other tests based on differential diagnosis or comorbidities. Not everyone needs every test.

ADA 2026 glycaemic thresholds (non-pregnant adults)

TestNormalPrediabetesDiabetes
HbA1c<5.7%5.7–6.4%≥6.5%
FPG<100 mg/dL100–125 mg/dL≥126 mg/dL
2-h 75-g OGTT<140 mg/dL140–199 mg/dL≥200 mg/dL

Sources: ADA Standards of Care 2026 · Diagnosis · NIDDK · Diabetes tests.

Anthropometry + metabolic estimates

Clinical Calculators

Interactive educational calculations — adult screening tools, not diagnosis.

1 · BMI (Body Mass Index)

Enter weight and height.

Adult WHO BMI categories: underweight <18.5 · healthy range 18.5–24.9 · overweight 25–29.9 · obesity ≥30 kg/m². Use age-specific growth charts for children/adolescents; pregnancy and high muscularity need different interpretation.

2 · Waist Circumference (WC) & Waist-to-Height Ratio (WHtR)

Enter waist and height.

Measure midway between the lowest palpable rib and the top of the iliac crest, standing, tape horizontal, after a normal expiration. Thresholds differ by sex and ethnicity; ADA 2026 commonly uses WC ≥88 cm women / ≥102 cm men for non-Asian backgrounds and ≥80 / ≥90 cm for Asian backgrounds. WHtR ≥0.5 is a useful screening flag, not a diagnosis.

3 · HOMA-IR (Homeostatic Model Assessment)

Enter fasting values.

HOMA1-IR = fasting insulin × fasting glucose / 405 (glucose mg/dL), or /22.5 (glucose mmol/L). This is a surrogate estimate, not a universal diagnostic cut-off. Requires genuinely fasting paired measurements and assay-specific context. Not validated for every clinical situation (e.g., exogenous insulin, pregnancy, acute illness).

4 · Estimated energy needs (Mifflin–St Jeor)

Enter adult data.

Equation estimates resting energy expenditure; activity multiplier estimates TDEE. It is not an individual prescription and may be inaccurate in pregnancy, illness, extremes of body composition or other special populations. A dietitian should individualise energy targets.

All calculations are for adult education and screening only. Results must be interpreted with clinical history, examination, laboratory methods, age, sex, ethnicity and comorbidities. Do not use these calculators to self-diagnose or change medication.

Egyptian whole-wheat baladi bread (عيش بلدي صحي)

تصحيح الاسم: عيش الطابونة اللي تقصديه هو العيش البلدي المصري 😄. اقتراح وصفة منزلية بسيطة: whole-wheat flour + bran (اختياري) + water + yeast + pinch of salt. اعتمدي على دقيق قمح كامل، وقللي/احذفي السكر والزيت غير الضروريين؛ ده لا يجعل الرغيف “مفتوح الكمية” — portion size still matters.

  1. اخلطي 4 أكواب دقيق قمح كامل مع ملعقة كبيرة خميرة فورية ونصف ملعقة صغيرة ملح.
  2. أضيفي حوالي 2¼ كوب ماء دافئ تدريجيًا واعجني لحد عجينة طرية.
  3. غطيها واتركيها تختمر قرابة ساعة، ثم قسّميها كور وافرديها أرغفة.
  4. اتركيها ترتاح قليلًا، ثم اخبزيها على صاج/طاسة ساخنة أو في فرن ساخن حتى تنتفخ وتنضج.

Watch: Egyptian whole-wheat baladi bread video ↗ · Alternative soft whole-wheat baladi bread ↗

Video recipes are user-generated, not clinical evidence. For nutrition calculation, weigh the baked loaf and calculate the full recipe from flour, oil, seeds and other ingredients; calories per loaf depend on final weight and recipe.

Important: recipe, oil quantity, bakery size, filling, cooking method and water loss change nutrition values. The listed weight is the edible serving weight, not a universal restaurant portion. Weigh your own serving and use product labels or a recipe calculation for precision. Macro values are rounded estimates; micronutrients are not fully listed.

Data basis: Egyptian Baladi bread composition study and USDA FoodData Central-derived reference values; mixed dishes use approximate recipe-based estimates. Baladi bread composition study (2015) · USDA FoodData Central · Egyptian food serving reference.

QR codes are intentionally compact and open curated search pages; check app permissions, privacy and accessibility before installing.

Weekly target

Adults: 150–300 min moderate aerobic activity (or 75–150 min vigorous), plus strength work ≥2 days/week, as tolerated.

Why movement helps

Muscle contraction supports glucose uptake, cardiorespiratory fitness, function and wellbeing, even when weight does not change.

Safety

Stop for chest pain, faintness, severe breathlessness or unusual symptoms. Seek clinical advice before vigorous exercise if you have relevant conditions.

WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour

Seafood · Mediterranean

Anti-Inflammatory Mediterranean Tuna Salad

A fresh, protein-rich salad with tuna, vegetables, herbs and a lemon–olive oil dressing.

⏱ 15 min · No cooking🍽 2 servings (estimate)
Estimated energy≈ 220–330 kcal
View ingredients & preparation

Ingredients

  • Tuna
  • Olive oil
  • Cucumber
  • Tomatoes
  • Fresh herbs
  • Lemon juice

Method

  1. Drain the tuna and flake it into a bowl.
  2. Chop the cucumber and tomatoes; add them with the herbs.
  3. Whisk olive oil with lemon juice, then toss gently with the salad.
  4. Serve chilled.

Calories are a rough estimate because ingredient quantities were not supplied; olive oil amount and tuna packed in water or oil will change the value.

Chicken · Creamy skillet

Creamy Garlic Parmesan Chicken Breast

Golden chicken breast finished in a garlic, cream and Parmesan sauce.

⏱ 30 min · Stovetop🍽 2 servings (estimate)
Estimated energy≈ 880 kcal
View ingredients & preparation

Ingredients

  • 2 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 2 tbsp butter
  • 4 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 cup heavy cream
  • ½ cup grated Parmesan cheese
  • 1 tsp Italian seasoning
  • Salt and black pepper, to taste
  • Fresh chopped parsley (optional)

Method

  1. Slice the chicken breasts in half and season with salt, pepper and Italian seasoning.
  2. Sear in olive oil until golden and cooked through; set aside.
  3. Add butter and garlic to the skillet and sauté until fragrant.
  4. Pour in the heavy cream and Parmesan; simmer until thickened.
  5. Return the chicken to the skillet and coat with the sauce. Garnish with parsley.

Approximate per serving, assuming the recipe makes 2 servings. Actual values vary with chicken size, cream and Parmesan brands.

Chicken · Oven-baked

Melt-in-Your-Mouth Parmesan Chicken

Oven-baked chicken topped with a creamy mayonnaise and Parmesan mixture.

⏱ 45 min · Oven🍽 4 servings (estimate)
Estimated energy≈ 665 kcal
View ingredients & preparation

Ingredients

  • 4 boneless chicken breasts
  • 1 cup mayonnaise
  • ½ cup grated Parmesan cheese
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1½ tsp seasoning salt
  • ½ tsp black pepper

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. Mix mayonnaise, Parmesan, garlic powder, seasoning salt and black pepper.
  3. Arrange chicken breasts in a baking dish and spread the mixture over them.
  4. Bake for about 45 minutes, until the chicken is fully cooked.

Approximate per serving, assuming 4 equal servings and the quantities shown in the image. Cooking time depends on breast thickness; cook poultry to a safe internal temperature.

Vegetarian · Oven-roasted

Roasted Veggie Delight

A colorful tray of potatoes, carrots and zucchini tossed with olive oil and herbs.

⏱ About 35–45 min · Oven🍽 4 servings (estimate)
Estimated energy≈ 250 kcal
View ingredients & preparation

Ingredients

  • 4 cups diced potatoes
  • 2 cups sliced carrots
  • 2 cups sliced zucchini
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1 tsp Italian seasoning
  • ½ tsp salt
  • ½ tsp black pepper

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
  2. Combine potatoes, carrots and zucchini in a large bowl.
  3. Drizzle with olive oil and toss to coat evenly.
  4. Add garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt and black pepper; mix well.
  5. Spread the vegetables in a single layer on a baking tray and roast until tender and lightly browned, turning once.

Approximate per serving, assuming 4 servings. The supplied image cuts off the final roasting instruction, so check tenderness as it cooks.

Chicken · Lemon & garlic

Easy Garlic Butter Chicken

Pan-seared chicken finished in a buttery garlic and lemon sauce.

⏱ 25–30 min · Stovetop🍽 4 servings (estimate)
Estimated energy≈ 370 kcal
View ingredients & preparation

Ingredients

  • 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 3 tbsp butter
  • 4 garlic cloves, minced
  • ½ cup chicken broth
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • Salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika, to season
  • Chopped parsley, to garnish

Method

  1. Season chicken with salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika.
  2. Heat olive oil in a skillet. Cook chicken for about 4–5 minutes per side until browned and cooked through; set aside.
  3. Add butter and minced garlic to the skillet.
  4. Stir in chicken broth and lemon juice.
  5. Return chicken to the pan and simmer in the sauce for 5–7 minutes.
  6. Garnish with chopped parsley and serve.

Approximate per serving, assuming 4 equal servings. Chicken size and the amount of butter/oil remaining in the pan affect the final value.

About the calorie estimates

Values are approximate, not laboratory measurements. They depend on ingredient brands, exact quantities, chicken size, cooking method and serving count. Where the supplied image did not include a complete ingredient list or quantities, a reliable recipe total cannot be calculated; this is stated on that recipe. These estimates are for food information, not personal diet targets.

1 · Search across trusted sources

اكتبي سؤالك بالعربي أو English، وبعدها افتحي قواعد البيانات والمصادر العلمية. كل مصدر يفتح بحثًا مستقلًا بنفس السؤال؛ لا يوجد في هذا prototype اتصال مباشر يجمع كل النتائج أو يراجعها تلقائيًا.

Evidence workflow: prioritise clinical guidelines and systematic reviews; check publication date, study design, population, conflicts of interest and whether findings apply to the question. A search result is not automatically a reliable conclusion.

2 · Nutrition Pharmacy Assistant

اسألي عن nutrition assessment، obesity، insulin resistance، meal composition، lab tests، أو medication-related nutrition questions.

Hello! أنا مساعد تعليمي في Clinical Nutrition. أقدر أوضح المفاهيم الأساسية وأساعدك تفهمي التحاليل والتغذية. اسأليني بالعربي أو English.

A production AI assistant needs a secure AI/API backend, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over vetted sources, citations, clinical safety filters, privacy controls and human escalation.
